It's depending on which period since each party did went through some form of evolution. But i'd assume you are talking about the seventh party system? In that case:

Conservatives advocate for Globalism, Internationalism, Economic Liberalism, and Liberal Conservatism. Unlike most parties, they favor smaller (and probably active) government with minimal micromanagement as safe as possible. I personally think of them as a mix of Rockefeller Republicans and New Democrats (as they are a mix of both parties anyways), but they probably grew to represent whats left of any right-wingers in seventh party system.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Republican

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democrats

Progressives advocate for Social Democracy, Progressivism, Economic Nationalism, etc. I assumed their policies are similar to Bernie Sanders or Elizabeth Warren (since I assume they led the Progressives before they were a separate party)

Labor is pretty similar to Progressives, but i think they are generally more conservative and more centre-left than Progressives. They probably aren't but thats my view of them

yeah, im probably not the best person to explain since we don't have all the info for each party on this wiki
